title: Connected workflows: Context turns answers into firm value
desc: Locates differentiation in proprietary data, integration and proactive assistance, while extending saved capacity toward revenue without proving autonomy.

kps.k: The central proposition is that legal AI gains value from connected workflows and firm-specific context, not just standalone answers.
kps.d: The Litera and Filevine accounts position broad software platforms as a foundation for useful AI assistance. Marwaha emphasises connecting drafting, experience management and client relationship information inside Word, Outlook and a web interface. The Filevine interview stresses shared needs across practices—documents, tasks, templates, reporting and calendars—and argues that matter history, participants, deadlines and communications enable relevant next-step guidance. These are vendor strategies and reported use cases, not comparative evidence that broad platforms outperform specialist tools.

qs.q: We harness some of the most critical experience from prior work and with CRM looking at the future work and using all that to present the right data at the right place at the right time for associates, partners, and rainmakers of law firms.

qs.q: So generally we want to be able to as uh broad a segment of the legal community as possible, mostly because we do think that a lot of legal work does overlap.
qs.a: From Customer to Acquirer: Filevine's Ryan Anderson and Pincites' Sona Sulakian on Building AI Contract Intelligence · Legal-tech vendor · 2026

kps.k: Proprietary data and familiar interfaces underpin the proposed differentiation and adoption benefits.
kps.d: Marwaha prioritises internal and client data over public information, arguing that firms differentiate through their own experience and lawyers’ expertise as shared software becomes standardised. He estimates that fragmented workflows require switching between 10 and 30 windows and credits earlier Word integration with adoption and business growth, without providing measured outcomes. His contrast with public-data-led vendors expresses a strategic disagreement; the supplied material contains no direct rebuttal or comparative test. Specialist teams may still prefer dedicated applications.

qs.q: And to me, right data is always internal data and client data first, public data second.
qs.a: Ep 293: Litera's Avaneesh Marwaha: The CEO Who Left Before AI and Returned to Lead Through It · Legal-tech vendor · 2025

qs.q: But when everybody has harmonized data, harmonized software, your data and the brains of partners and associates is what's differentiating.
qs.a: Ep 293: Litera's Avaneesh Marwaha: The CEO Who Left Before AI and Returned to Lead Through It · Legal-tech vendor · 2025

kps.k: Proactive assistance aims to remove retrieval and handoff work, but the examples do not establish autonomous legal delivery.
kps.d: Marwaha describes an email-triggered agent that finds an earlier document version and prepares a comparison, risk analysis and change summary in Outlook. He also describes retrieving relevant firm experience directly from a client request. His claimed 20-minute saving lacks a measurement method. The Filevine interview reports customers using Lois to understand matter status and then copying information into subsequent drafting work. That observation identifies a remaining workflow handoff rather than demonstrating independent task completion. Neither account supplies independent accuracy or end-to-end productivity evidence.

qs.q: So for example, opposing counsel sends you an email with version 12, Lido, our GNI agent, can look at the email and look for version 11 and give you a comparison waiting for you.
qs.a: The Business of Law: From IP Lawyer to Investor to CEO to Legal Tech Ecosystem Builder (Avaneesh Marwaha, Litera CEO) · Legal-tech vendor · 2025

qs.q: Well, increasingly we have seen that at that point, the customer then takes that data out of Lois and cuts and pastes it into work.
qs.a: From Customer to Acquirer: Filevine's Ryan Anderson and Pincites' Sona Sulakian on Building AI Contract Intelligence · Legal-tech vendor · 2026

kps.k: Litera extends the efficiency argument into revenue generation: firms should use released capacity to win additional matters.
kps.d: Marwaha shifts attention beyond associate drafting toward partners, business development and proactive client communication. He argues that automation creates spare capacity that firms must fill, assuming clients already hold additional matters. He predicts stronger competition within 24 months of the interview as smaller firms and sole practitioners expand their business-development capacity and take work from incumbent large firms. These are commercial recommendations and forecasts, not demonstrated revenue effects; his account of receiving no partner outreach over a decade offers personal anecdotal support rather than a market-wide finding.

qs.q: Going forward, at least my brain power is on Rainmakers and partners and business development folks, because I think top-line growth is more important all of a sudden.
qs.a: Ep 293: Litera's Avaneesh Marwaha: The CEO Who Left Before AI and Returned to Lead Through It · Legal-tech vendor · 2025

qs.q: I think as mid-market law firms and sole practitioners lean into GENAI, their capacity to BD will increase.
qs.a: The Business of Law: From IP Lawyer to Investor to CEO to Legal Tech Ecosystem Builder (Avaneesh Marwaha, Litera CEO) · Legal-tech vendor · 2025

kps.k: Integration requires data preparation, organisational change and accommodation of competing products.
kps.d: Marwaha says large implementations need data cleanup and remapping, specialist consulting, training and change management, with Litera retaining a support role. He endorses interoperability when firms select competitors, while acknowledging that third-party connections may offer less functionality than native Litera integrations. This qualifies the unified-platform ambition: firms must plan for implementation effort and mixed software estates, not installation alone. His confidence in Microsoft’s security and the separate podcast host’s claim that fuller AI capability requires cloud adoption remain assertions rather than demonstrated technical findings.

qs.q: It requires a lot of data visualization and remapping and clean up.

qs.q: I believe in the safety and security of a Microsoft brings to enterprise-grade organizations.

vlens.an: The curated legal-tech-vendor sources support the proposition that legal AI creates firm value chiefly when embedded in connected workflows and supplied with proprietary, matter-specific context, rather than used only for isolated answers. Their common reasoning is that useful assistance depends on bringing together documents, communications, deadlines, prior work, experience and CRM data, then presenting relevant outputs inside familiar environments such as Word and Outlook. Material variation concerns emphasis: Filevine focuses on broad shared workflow needs and the matter context required for next-step guidance, while its reported copy-and-paste handoff indicates continued human workflow rather than autonomous legal delivery. Litera places greater weight on ecosystem integration, proactive retrieval and using AI-released capacity for business development and new-matter growth; it also stresses data preparation, change management and interoperability. These commercial and productivity claims are largely vendor-reported examples, recommendations and forecasts, not independent comparative or end-to-end performance evidence. The sources therefore support the proposition and its qualifications, but this curated selection should not be treated as representative of legal-tech vendors generally.

qs.q: But in the world of legal AI, what really matters is having all that context so that you can start taking agent at work.

elens.an: The 2025 sources support the proposition that legal AI produces greater firm value when embedded in connected workflows, informed by proprietary firm and client data, and delivered through familiar interfaces rather than as isolated answers. Across both interviews, Marwaha’s common reasoning is that integration reduces context switching, combines drafting, experience and CRM information, and enables proactive retrieval or workflow assistance. The sources also support the proposition’s commercial extension: capacity released through automation should be redirected toward client service, business development and additional matters. Material variation lies mainly in emphasis. One interview focuses on proactive agentic workflow examples and forecasts increased competition for client matters; the other gives more attention to internal-data differentiation, interface consolidation, interoperability, data preparation and change management. These implementation qualifications do not undermine the core proposition. However, both records largely present the strategy and claims of the same vendor executive, not independent comparative evidence: reported adoption, time savings and anticipated revenue effects are not supported here by disclosed measurement methods, and the examples do not establish autonomous legal delivery.

qs.q: Today, more than last year, they get a significant value from that because we can now touch all those things in a workflow in a very unified front-end, so it feels harmonious that you're using one tool to get your answers.

elens.an: The 2026 Filevine source supports the principal proposition that legal AI derives value from connected workflows and matter-specific context rather than standalone answers. It links broad platform coverage to recurring workflow needs across legal practice—documents, tasks, drafting, templates, reporting and calendars—and argues that useful next-step guidance depends on matter history, participants, progress, deadlines, events, documents and emails. Materially, however, the source offers reported customer interactions rather than comparative or quantified evidence that broad platforms outperform specialist tools. Its account of users copying information from Lois into later work also supports the synthesis’s limit: contextual assistance may improve retrieval and decision support, but the example retains a manual handoff and does not establish autonomous end-to-end legal delivery. The source does not address the synthesis’s additional claims about proprietary data as competitive differentiation, implementation and change-management requirements, or converting released capacity into revenue.
